Task: implement the fixes from an Impeccable critique of the reader and reply/compose UI of Email OS (Vue 3 + Tauri desktop email client), in five steps (layout, clarify, polish a11y/affordances, typeset, final polish). The critique scored the area 28/40 (was 22/40; inbox/search is 35/40). It was done from source only (no browser, no node_modules, nothing rendered), so VERIFY every claim by reading the code and reproducing it in a test before fixing; if a claim is wrong, say so and skip it.

Read PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md (read fully) first. Brand: focused, precise, trustworthy; keyboard-first; honest state; message content renders as safe literal plain text; drafts local-only; no Send by design; anti-references: Gmail clutter, AI magic, generic SaaS cards, optimistic UI that lies. Mode is Operate (app UI): consistency, density and native expectations outrank expression. The Impeccable skill is installed at ~/.claude/skills/impeccable (SKILL.md and reference/*.md; its launcher is ~/.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable). Use it: run `~/.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable context --target src/components/ReaderView.vue` once, then follow reference/layout.md, clarify.md, polish.md and typeset.md for the respective steps, and read reference/craft-floor.md immediately before editing UI. `impeccable detect --json <files>` is available for a deterministic scan (the reader/compose .vue files currently scan clean; style.css has 6 known pre-existing advisories outside this area). Ignore the 'CONTEXT_STALE' notes about PRODUCT.md/design.json drift; do not repair them. Also read the repo's `implement` skill / persona-feature-engineer agent and use it for implementation, test-first.

Out of scope: DRAFT INTEGRITY (the P1 about R then Esc leaving blank drafts / resuming drafts / a 'Draft' marker in the reader status line) is explicitly deferred; do not change draft creation, dedupe or cleanup behaviour. Also out of scope: a provider handoff / 'Open in provider' (local drafts stay as they are), the drawer panels (DraftsPanel, ActivityPanel, RemindersPanel, CachedTrashPanel; another thread, branch impeccable/drawer-panels, may be touching them and DraftsPanel embeds DraftEditorCore, so keep DraftEditorCore API-compatible and changes there minimal), AccountPanel/ProviderDestinations/first-run (another thread, impeccable/account-first-run), search, bulk selection bar/notice dock. Rebase on origin/main if conflicts appear; main has moved (reminders PR #33).

Steps, with findings (file:line refs are from the review; re-find them):

Step 2 LAYOUT (P2). Reader geometry is off the product grid. `.reader-pane` uses `padding: .5rem .75rem` (style.css ~1319-1323), so the subject starts near 12px while the header title and the inbox list sit on the 50px inset; opening a row visibly shifts the text edge. The undocked compose card uses the 50px margin (~2284) but the docked one uses 0 (~2300). Put the reader on the 50px inset (decide the right edge deliberately and keep long-line measure at 65ch), make docked/undocked compose margins agree, and fix the loading skeleton row height (style.css ~1418-1421 uses 1.4em while its comment says the collapsed height is 2em, so the pane may still jump). Keep J/K reader navigation smooth with no empty frame. Reconcile DESIGN.md gap 16 and the reader geometry docs.

Step 3 CLARIFY (P2). (a) The reply heading is always `Reply draft to {From name}` (ReplyComposer.vue ~111), but To defaults from Reply-To (generated.ts ~426; draft_core.rs ~376), so on list/newsletter/support-desk mail the heading and the To row disagree and Cc/Subject auto-open (DraftEditorCore ~135, ~159). Derive the heading from the actual To (or add a terse 'Reply-To differs' line) and verify the compact form still holds when Reply-To differs. (b) The Message DTO has no Cc: the reader shows `to X, Y` (ReaderView ~1017) and Details lists From/To/Sent only (~1050-1082), so a Cc'd thread looks complete and a reply silently drops people. Say so plainly and tersely, e.g. 'Cc not cached' where Cc is unknown; do not fabricate Cc and do not change the wire format unless trivial and safe. (c) Replace the internal 'Prepare reply' wording with plain 'Reply' in titles, labels, palette and tests, keeping the R hint. (d) `describeError` leaks `invalid field:` (ReaderView ~204): replace with a plain message. (e) AttachmentChooser empty state is a ~230-char line (AttachmentChooser.vue ~86) and uses 'Known files' jargon: shorten to terse factual copy. Voice: terse, factual, sentence-case, no exclamation marks.

Step 4 POLISH: affordances and accessibility (P2). (a) The composer field underline (Seam #474543) is 1.36:1 on the raised surface and is the only at-rest cue that an empty field is an input; raise it to >=3:1 or add a second at-rest cue, staying within DESIGN.md tokens (add a token only if needed and document it). (b) `.composer-caveat-toggle` is ~18x18px; enlarge the hit area (not necessarily the glyph). (c) `.participant` spans in the reader (ReaderView ~1054, ~1071) are role-less `tabindex=0` with a colour-only/dotted-underline focus style and add a tab stop per recipient: either give them a real visible focus ring and a role, or remove the extra tab stops (the full address must stay reachable by keyboard and screen reader). (d) AttachmentChooser buttons all read 'Save to Downloads' (~83): give each a per-file accessible label like the inline ones. Align inline 'Save' vs chooser 'Save to Downloads' wording. (e) MessageAttachments 'Could not load file details.' (~62) has no retry: add a Retry action. (f) The `▸` in Details is generated CSS (style.css ~1641): make sure state is exposed to assistive tech (aria-expanded or native details semantics). Do not use Graphite (#8e8a87) for meaningful glyphs on focus-fill (2.75:1). Keep every existing live region quiet (status line announces only meaningful transitions).

Step 5 TYPESET (P2). (a) The quote attribution pattern is English-only (message-body-format.ts ~42), so 'Le ... a écrit :' / 'Am ... schrieb ...' / 'El ... escribió:' etc. quotes never collapse: broaden it safely (still plain text, lossless, no HTML), with tests. (b) Any interleaved `>` line in the prose forces the whole body to monospace at 13.6px (message-body-format.ts ~12-17, documented limitation): fix if small and safe (e.g. only force mono when the non-quoted prose itself looks tabular/aligned), otherwise keep the limitation and document it. (c) The 15px reading size (`--type-reading`, style.css ~27) is not in DESIGN.md's scale: document the reading type role (size, line-height 1.6, 65ch measure, mono fallback) in DESIGN.md. (d) Review hierarchy in the reader: 16px/600 subject over 15px/400 body leans on weight alone; adjust only if a measured, small change fixes it, otherwise leave and say why. (e) quotedSnippet slices at 200 UTF-16 units (App.vue ~441), which can split a surrogate pair and previews the raw head; slice by code points/grapheme boundary.

Step 6 POLISH final. Run the detector on the touched files, a CSS hygiene pass (no hardcoded colours, tokens only, on-scale spacing/radii, focus-visible on every new interactive element), re-check DESIGN.md/docs for claims that changed, make sure nothing from steps 2-5 regressed editable/IME shortcut protection, announcements, focus handling, reduced-motion or J/K smoothness. Minor leftovers to fold in if trivial: `.reader-pending` should be a status role; chooser 'Known files' jargon; up to 20 Reply-To recipients in a single-line input (check layout only).

Constraints: honour PRODUCT.md 'Standing constraints'; no HTML rendering of message content; no auto-open of attachments; no optimistic UI; no real provider writes. Copy terse, sentence-case.

Process: run `pnpm install` if node_modules is missing, then add failing tests first for each verified issue, fix, and run the project's checks (see mise.toml and docs/development.md; lint, typecheck, vitest). Commit per step with clear messages on this branch, update DESIGN.md/docs where behaviour or claims changed, add a short note to the reader/compose critique files under .impeccable/critique/ (create a new file in the existing format if the previous ones are not on your branch), and open ONE PR to main. Report back: what you changed per step, what you verified and how, what you rejected or could not verify (e.g. no rendered screenshots; say whether you were able to run the app or take any), and anything deferred.
I'll start by reading the product docs, the skills and the repo layout.

---
name: implement
description: Implement an Email OS feature, bug fix, or approved plan from a task description or repository document. Use when asked to implement a scoped change in this repo. Delegates implementation to the local persona-feature-engineer agent.
---

# Implement

Implement the requested change in Email OS. The request can be a task description, an approved plan, or a path to a repository document with a specific item to implement. No ticket service is required.

Usage: `/skill:implement <task description or document path and item>`

All repository paths below are relative to the repository root. The local persona definition is `.pi/agents/persona-feature-engineer.md` from the repository root. Runtimes that mirror these documents through symlinks keep this path authoritative; follow the target, not the mirror location.

## 1. Establish the task

- Read the request and referenced documents. Identify the goal, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and affected code.
- If the request names a broad document, ask which item to implement. Do not treat every proposed feature in that document as approved work.
- Ask for clarification if a product, architecture, data migration, or scope decision is missing. Do not invent requirements.
- Inspect the working-tree status. Preserve pre-existing edits and keep one writer per checkout.

## 2. Gather repository context

Use local code and documentation, not external wiki or code-graph services:

- `README.md` for the project entry points and document map.
- `docs/development.md` for setup, commands, profile isolation, and validation gates.
- `docs/adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md` for accepted first-build scope.
- The relevant slice or UX contract under `docs/`, and the relevant section of `docs/superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md` or `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md` for browsing work.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` only as a proposal, not as an inventory of implemented behavior. The PRD and older research do not authorize scope expansion.
- Current code and tests to confirm actual behavior. Escalate material conflicts between the task, accepted contracts, and implementation.

Find the affected seam:

- `crates/mail-core/`: Rust mail core, DTOs, SQLite, Gmail auth/provider/cache/sync/actions.
- `src/` and `tests/`: Vue 3/TypeScript UI, IPC adapter, and frontend tests.
- `src-tauri/`: thin Tauri 2 native shell and command/event bridge.
- `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts`: generated wire contract. Never edit it by hand; change the Rust DTOs and run `mise run gen:ts`.

Follow existing conventions and any applicable project instructions. Do not invent a separate coding-standard source.

## 3. Delegate implementation

Using this skill authorizes one implementation subagent. Do not ask the user to request delegation again.

- Read your runtime's subagent guidance and the local persona definition before launch.
- Launch `persona-feature-engineer` with whatever subagent or delegation mechanism your own runtime provides (a native subagent tool, a task tool, a delegate API — the choice is yours and not prescribed here). Inherit the parent model unless the user specifies another one.
- Give the child a self-contained brief: explicit repository cwd, goal, acceptance criteria, non-goals, relevant files and contracts, pre-existing edits, edit boundary, required checks, verification method, and expected evidence.
- Tell the child to execute directly. It must not use this skill to delegate again or start other agents.
- Leave implementation to the child. Do not edit the same checkout while it works. Follow native async completion notifications; do not poll or sleep.
- Route blocking decisions to the user when the task and project instructions do not already answer them. Do not approve new scope on the user's behalf.

If subagent tooling is unavailable before launch, read the persona definition and do the work directly under its rules. State that fallback. If a launch or runtime fails, stop and report the failure and partial work state. Do not silently switch execution methods.

If you are already the delegated implementation child, follow the persona and execute the task directly. Do not launch another agent.

## 4. Test and verify

Use `mise.toml` and `docs/development.md` as the command source. Select the checks that cover the changed seam:

| Change | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Rust mail core | `mise run test:core`, `mise run lint:core` |
| Rust DTOs or IPC | Regenerate with `mise run gen:ts`; run `mise run check:contract`, core tests, and affected UI/native checks |
| Vue/TypeScript UI | `mise run test:ui`, `mise run typecheck`, `mise run build:web` |
| Tauri shell or bridge | `mise run check:native`, `mise run test:native`, plus affected core/UI checks |
| Cross-cutting work | `mise run check` plus web build and native checks where affected |

Add focused regression tests. Capture before-and-after behavior as required by the persona. Run the relevant checks against the final code and report exact commands and outcomes.

- Use `mise run dev:web` for the synthetic, in-memory browser preview. Use `mise run dev:native` for native fixture verification. Use a background terminal for long-running dev processes.
- Browser success is not proof of SQLite durability, native IPC, macOS WKWebView behavior, Keychain, OAuth, or Gmail convergence. Run the relevant native path or report the native gate as blocked and ask how to verify it.
- Default to synthetic fixtures and fake-provider tests. Do not enable Gmail mode, request OAuth grants, connect a real mailbox, or perform real provider writes without explicit operator approval for the disposable-account path.
- Never expose credentials or real mailbox content in logs, screenshots, or reports. Preserve profile isolation and existing permission boundaries.
- Do not install OS packages or change system configuration merely to unblock a native check. Report missing prerequisites.

## Rust dependency documentation

Check `Cargo.lock` for the exact resolved crate version before looking up its API. If multiple versions exist, identify the one used by the affected package. Do not use `latest` or change a dependency merely to match newer documentation.

- Item index: `https://docs.rs/{crate}/{version}/{crate_underscored}/all.html`
- Specific item: `https://docs.rs/{crate}/{version}/{crate_underscored}/struct.Foo.html` (or `trait.`, `enum.`, `fn.`)
- Source browser: `https://docs.rs/crate/{crate}/{version}/source/`

Use the same version-specific approach for frontend and Tauri documentation, based on `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `Cargo.lock`.

## 5. Return the result

Review the child's final diff and evidence against the task. Do not equate a successful agent exit with a verified feature. Report:

- What changed and which acceptance criteria it meets.
- Changed file paths.
- Exact checks and results, including failures or skipped gates.
- Before-and-after verification evidence and artifact paths.
- Remaining risks, blockers, and decisions needed.

Do not claim completion when required verification is missing. Do not commit, push, publish, or update a pull request unless the user authorizes it. Return pull-request-ready evidence when publication is not authorized.
---
name: persona-feature-engineer
description: Implement scoped features with focused tests and before-and-after verification evidence
advertise: true
acceptanceRole: writer
systemPromptMode: append
inheritProjectContext: true
inheritSkills: true
---

# Feature Engineer Persona

Work as a production engineer. Implement the assigned feature in the existing system. Meet the requirements and the applicable coding standards.

Write in the style of ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Use short sentences, direct instructions, and consistent terms. Preserve exact code identifiers, commands, and technical terms.

## Scope and authority

- Read the task, acceptance criteria, project instructions, and relevant code before you edit.
- Follow the coding standards for the project and language.
- If the code does not meet the requirements, change the code.
- Preserve existing user-visible and external behavior outside the task scope. Change existing behavior when the requirements call for it.
- Refactor production code when this makes the feature clear and maintainable. Do not preserve obsolete code only because it exists. Keep refactoring within the task scope.
- Do not add unrequested features, dependencies, abstractions, or cleanup.
- Make routine implementation choices within the approved requirements and project patterns. Do not invent product requirements or make unapproved architecture, public API, migration, or scope decisions.
- If requirements conflict or a decision is missing, stop the affected work and ask the supervisor. Do not guess.
- Do the assigned work yourself. Do not start other subagents unless the parent explicitly authorizes delegation.

## Gather information

Use the sources that apply to the task:

- The task brief and project instructions.
- Relevant code, tests, local documentation, and coding-standard rules.
- The Tolaria wiki for documented behavior, when it is available and relevant.
- The Frontier Platform CodeGraph for code relationships, when it is available and relevant.

Check documentation against the current code. Do not assume that an unavailable source was checked. If a missing source blocks a correct implementation, ask for access or the required information. Otherwise, state the limitation and continue with the available evidence.

## Implement and test

1. Define the expected result from the acceptance criteria.
2. Capture the before state before you edit production code.
3. Make a focused, coherent change. Follow the existing project patterns.
4. Add or update short, focused automated tests. Cover the requested behavior, relevant failure cases, and behavior that must stay unchanged.
5. Run the relevant tests, type checks, lint checks, and build checks available in the project. Do not weaken tests or checks to make the change pass.
6. Verify the feature through its user-facing or external interface.
7. Review the final diff for scope, correctness, and unrelated changes.

Use automated tests to prove behavior. Manual checks do not replace tests. Passing tests alone do not replace verification through the actual interface.

## Verify the change

Work without verification is not done. Capture a comparable before state and after state. If the feature does not exist before the change, record its absence or the current failure.

- **UI change:** Run the app or Storybook. Use the affected flow. Capture screenshots before and after the change.
- **Backend or CLI change:** Call the endpoint or run the command. Record the inputs, relevant environment, exit status or HTTP status, and returned output before and after the change.
- **Prompt or eval change:** Run the relevant evals before and after the change. Record the configuration and both results.
- **Other change:** Use the actual consumer or execution path. Record reproducible before-and-after evidence.

Use safe local or test data. Do not mutate production systems, send messages, or perform destructive operations without explicit approval. Remove secrets and personal data from evidence.

Capture the after state when the tests pass. If you change the code after verification, rerun the affected checks and capture new after evidence. Replace evidence that no longer represents the final code.

If you cannot capture the baseline or run the change, stop and ask how to verify it. Do not claim the work is done or fabricate evidence.

## Escalation

Follow the runtime's supervisor-routing instructions. When available, use `contact_supervisor` with `reason: "need_decision"` for a blocking question. State the blocker, the decision needed, and the relevant options. Wait for the answer before you continue the affected work.

If the supervisor tool is unavailable, return a blocked result with the question and current work state. Do not report success.

## Guardrails

- Do not inspect Git history. Do not use history, blame, or old revisions to investigate past changes. You may use Git status and working-tree diffs to inspect current work.
- Preserve unrelated and pre-existing edits. Do not reset, discard, or overwrite another contributor's work.
- Do not commit, push, open or update a merge request, or publish changes unless the task authorizes it.
- Follow inherited tool, safety, and project instructions. This persona does not expand your permissions.

## Result and evidence

Return a concise handoff:

- **Status:** complete or blocked.
- **Implemented:** what changed and which requirements it meets.
- **Files:** changed file paths.
- **Checks:** exact commands, results, and any failures or skipped checks.
- **Verification:** before-and-after observations, relevant outputs, and screenshot or artifact paths.
- **Risks or blockers:** remaining limitations and required decisions.

Put verification evidence in the merge request description, not in a comment, when the task authorizes a merge request update. Otherwise, return merge-request-ready evidence to the parent. Do not create or update a merge request only to store evidence.

1	# Product
2	
3	## Register
4	
5	product
6	
7	## Users
8	
9	Initially a single person: the author, dogfooding a single-account desktop client (macOS first) against their own Gmail inbox in focused, keyboard-first sessions. They move through a high volume of mail quickly, want to reach "done" on each conversation, and need to trust that every action (archive, bulk processing, undo, send) did exactly what it claimed. The provider's own client remains the fallback.
10	
11	Longer term: technically capable people who want to compose their own email workflow (custom views, triage signals, commands, automations), manually or with an agent, without rebuilding sync, credentials, or send safety.
12	
13	The primary task on most screens is triage: scan the list, open a conversation, decide, act, move on.
14	
15	## Product Purpose
16	
17	A composable email client: a trusted mail engine (sync, safe rendering, credentials, action execution) with replaceable signals, views, commands, and workflows on top. It ships an opinionated reference experience, a compact Superhuman-style browsing and keyboard flow, rather than a blank toolkit.
18	
19	The near-term goal is a complete, trustworthy inbox-processing session. Strategic scope is set by `docs/adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md` and `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md`; this file does not expand it.
20	
21	Success looks like: the author processes their inbox faster and with more confidence than in their previous client, and every automated or bulk action is previewable, reported honestly (including partial success and "outcome unknown"), and undoable where undo is real.
22	
23	## Brand Personality
24	
25	**Focused, precise, trustworthy.**
26	
27	- **Focused:** the interface recedes so the mail and the next decision are what's on screen. Dense, quiet, few competing elements.
28	- **Precise:** exact states, exact counts, exact wording. No vague "something went wrong", no rounded-off truth about what happened.
29	- **Trustworthy:** the client never overstates what it did. Pending, failed, partial, and ambiguous outcomes are visible and distinct. Automation shows its work before it acts.
30	
31	Voice is terse and factual: short labels, plain verbs, no exclamation marks, no cheerleading.
32	
33	## Anti-references
34	
35	- **Gmail-web clutter:** toolbars of rarely-used icons, chrome competing with content, permanent competing panels.
36	- **"AI magic" email products:** AI destinations, sparkle icons, generated summaries presented as fact, fabricated contact enrichment, automation that acts without a preview.
37	- **Superhuman feature-parity clone:** Superhuman is the visual and interaction reference for browsing (layout, density, type, keyboard feel), and close look parity there is a goal. Features and workflows are our own; don't import Superhuman's product scope or claim verified behavioral parity.
38	- **Generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics:** card stacks and grids, gradient heroes, oversized rounded panels, decorative illustration or motion.
39	- **Optimistic UI that lies:** "Done" before the provider confirmed, silent retries of ambiguous sends, dead controls that look actionable.
40	
41	## Design Principles
42	
43	1. **Honest state over smooth feel.** When speed and truthfulness conflict, show the truth. Every action has a visible pending, success, partial, failed, or unknown state. Show evidence and coverage, including unknown and retained facts.
44	2. **Keyboard first, mouse welcome.** Every core triage path is reachable and discoverable from the keyboard; pointer interaction is supported, never required.

Method: single-agent, code-and-test verification only. Nothing was rendered (no Chrome on this VM, no screenshots), so every visual claim below is read from CSS and templates, not measured. The prior whole-app review scored this area 22/40 and ranked it next (attention 8/10). ### 1. No reply shortcut — CONFIRMED, P1
`grep` finds no `r` binding anywhere in `App.vue`'s `onKeydown`, and `browsing-actions.ts` has no `reply` action. `prepareReply` (App.vue:1587) is reached only from `ReaderView` emitting `prepareReply`, from two controls: the header glyph `data-test="prepare-reply"` (ReaderView:710-720) and a per-message glyph on the active latest message (ReaderView:848-862). Reading is fully keyboard-driven (J/K/N/P/O/E/S/Z/C); replying is the one step that needs the pointer, which breaks "keyboard first" in the middle of the triage loop.
Safety already holds for a new key: the dispatcher returns for editable targets and IME (`isComposing`/`keyCode 229`, App.vue:1867-1869), returns early while a composer owns keys (App.vue:1866), and `actionShortcutBlocked` lets message toggles through but blocks other buttons. Reply must stay reader-only: the list holds no loaded message, so a list-level R would have to open, load and then reply, which is new scope. The source stays the displayed latest message (never the focused one), and the key must be unavailable for Cached Trash (`browsingOnly`), blocked replies (retained snapshot, incomplete, header mismatch), non-ready state and an open drawer.
Fix: add `reply` to `browsingActions` (label unchanged: "Prepare reply", shortcut R, so existing accessible names stay), `actionGroupOf`, `actionAliases` (respond, answer, write back), `actionAvailable`, `executeAction`, and the key handler; surface "R" in the header glyph title and palette; drive the reader's button titles from `actionLabel('reply')`.

### 2. Reply composer is a form — CONFIRMED, P1
`DraftEditorCore` renders four always-visible labelled fields (To, Cc, Subject, Body) in a 2-column grid (`.composer-fields`, style.css:1819), with a body that is `min-height: 8rem` (5rem when docked, style.css:2070). The core already pre-fills To and `Re: …` Subject for a reply (asserted in `reply-composer.component.test.ts:88-90`), so showing them as empty-looking boxes asks the user to re-read fields they never need to touch. Cc is optional and never filled for a reply. The new-message card needs To and Subject visible (they start empty) but Cc is rarely used.
Fix: reply surface gets a one-line recipient row ("To  Ada Fixture"), Cc and Subject behind a quiet "Cc / Subject" disclosure, and the body is the dominant, auto-focused field. New message keeps To and Subject visible and puts Cc on demand. The To row must never misrepresent the field: show the display name only while To is still the default sender mailbox, and the raw text once edited. Existing `data-test` hooks stay on the inputs; tests that read Cc or Subject reveal them first.
Quoted source: `.reply-quoted` is `--font-mono` at `--type-mono` (0.85rem), larger than the 12px shell and the proportional reading face above it (style.css, ReplyComposer.vue:154-165). Switch to the UI face at the body size in `--text-secondary` (4.99:1 on Focus Stone, ≥ 7:1 on `surface-raised`), keep the 2px rule and pre-wrap, keep it read-only and out of `bodyText`.

The drawer's own `draft-local-note` in `DraftsPanel` stays (a different surface), but the editor core no longer duplicates it.

Two are standing statements repeated on every open: "Opening this conversation does not change read state; use an explicit read control" (Gmail with actions) and "Read-only Gmail view: messages are never marked as read. Opening this conversation does not change read state." (Gmail read-only), plus the Cached Trash text. The rest are real exceptions and should stay.
Fix: one muted status line in the existing meta row ("Unread" / "Read-only · Unread"), with the full sentence in its `title` and as visually hidden text, so the guarantee stays discoverable without repeating on screen. Keep every exception inline and amber: reply blocked, retained snapshot, unsupported/incomplete, pending, star attention. Keep the `reader-readonly` / `reader-no-auto-read` hooks on the status line. The Trash notice drops its "Opening does not change read state." sentence and keeps what Trash actually restricts.

`bodyNeedsMonospace` returns true on the first line matching `^ {0,3}>`, so every reply-chain message renders entirely in mono (message-body-format.ts); two consecutive 4-space-indented lines (signatures, lists) do the same. The quoted tail is also what makes most real threads long.

Decide monospace from the prose part only, render signature and quote in the reading face in Ash, and put the quote behind a "Show quoted text" disclosure (per message, kept in the visit state so it survives J/K round trips). Still literal text via interpolation, the `>` characters are never rewritten, nothing is dropped, and interleaved (inline) quotes stay in place and keep the mono rule. The collapsed-row snippet uses the prose part so a message that is mostly quote does not preview as `>`.

Over-5-MiB files say "Over 5 MiB limit". # Development guide

This repository contains two deliberately separate native profiles: the durable
synthetic fixture slice (Slice 01) and an explicit Gmail profile built in stages.
Slice 02 adds system-browser OAuth/PKCE, a macOS Keychain credential store,
bounded inbox caching, and background sync. Slice 03 adds opt-in, durable Gmail
archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread actions; Gmail remains read-only until
the user explicitly requests the broader Google `gmail.modify` permission.
Slice 04 adds a local-only plain-text composer and durable draft recovery, but
still does not send/delete mail or expose arbitrary labels. Opening a message
never marks it read. UX-05 adds bounded multi-select and durable bulk
archive/read group processing with one-level partial group Undo; the browser
preview remains synthetic and in-memory. See
the slice contracts for individual acceptance scope. UX-08 adds narrow Gmail-mode
Star/Unstar singles/groups, durable Undo/reconciliation, cache-only Starred and a
single cached starred filter; see [its contract and validation ledger](ux-08-stars.md).
The legacy native fixture remains archive-only; unsupported star controls are
absent there. No real provider writes are authorized by implementation tests.
UX-06 adds one durable local
sender/domain split over Inbox, exact cached-count badges, and a single unread
filter. See [the saved-split contract](ux-06-saved-split.md) for matching,
keyboard navigation, cache coverage, and persistence boundaries.

| `src/`, `tests/`, `package.json`, configs | Vue 3/TypeScript frontend, IPC adapter and tests |
| `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts` | **Generated** — do not edit by hand; regenerate with `mise run gen:ts` |

| `mise.toml` | Project tasks (see below) |

## UX-09 increment A: read-only provider mail

The **Provider mail** rail entry (Gmail native or labelled browser preview) opens
a bounded destination browser for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash
and user labels. Search covers the loaded catalog; Show more expands it. It is
not mailbox search. All Mail excludes Spam/Trash. Every page contains at most
25 conversations, at most 16 MiB of serialized thread DTOs, and no exact total.
The read-only drawer intentionally has no triage/reply controls. Its page remains
mounted during a reader visit; closing the drawer returns to the prior inbox
context. This is not yet the roadmap's integrated main-list destination context.

Native commands `list_provider_destinations(accountId, cached)` and
`browse_provider_destination(request)` run off the UI thread, require the active
account, and use readonly Gmail APIs. Page cursors carry account+destination
identity and a bounded opaque provider token; they grant no authority.
A separate SQLite table retains one catalog and up to 20 destination snapshots
(latest successful page per retained destination), independent of inbox discovery,
history and operation recovery. **Use saved catalog/page** is explicit and
timestamped; provider failures are never silently converted to saved success or
an empty list. Restart retains these snapshots; disconnect clears them.

Provider Drafts are read-only snapshots, **not** the app's local editable drafts.
The native fixture rejects both provider commands; browser preview models them
in memory only. Label/Move, label badges on ordinary inbox rows, palette integration,
and saved-view/search criteria are not implemented here. After rebasing onto

increment. See [the increment contract](ux-09-provider-destinations.md)
for evidence and remaining gates.

# PRODUCT.md

# Product

## Register

product

## Users

Initially a single person: the author, dogfooding a single-account desktop client (macOS first) against their own Gmail inbox in focused, keyboard-first sessions. They move through a high volume of mail quickly, want to reach "done" on each conversation, and need to trust that every action (archive, bulk processing, undo, send) did exactly what it claimed. The provider's own client remains the fallback.

Longer term: technically capable people who want to compose their own email workflow (custom views, triage signals, commands, automations), manually or with an agent, without rebuilding sync, credentials, or send safety.

The primary task on most screens is triage: scan the list, open a conversation, decide, act, move on.

## Product Purpose

A composable email client: a trusted mail engine (sync, safe rendering, credentials, action execution) with replaceable signals, views, commands, and workflows on top. It ships an opinionated reference experience, a compact Superhuman-style browsing and keyboard flow, rather than a blank toolkit.

The near-term goal is a complete, trustworthy inbox-processing session. Strategic scope is set by `docs/adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md` and `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md`; this file does not expand it.

Success looks like: the author processes their inbox faster and with more confidence than in their previous client, and every automated or bulk action is previewable, reported honestly (including partial success and "outcome unknown"), and undoable where undo is real.

## Brand Personality

**Focused, precise, trustworthy.**

- **Focused:** the interface recedes so the mail and the next decision are what's on screen. Dense, quiet, few competing elements.
- **Precise:** exact states, exact counts, exact wording. No vague "something went wrong", no rounded-off truth about what happened.
- **Trustworthy:** the client never overstates what it did. Pending, failed, partial, and ambiguous outcomes are visible and distinct. Automation shows its work before it acts.

Voice is terse and factual: short labels, plain verbs, no exclamation marks, no cheerleading.

## Anti-references

- **Gmail-web clutter:** toolbars of rarely-used icons, chrome competing with content, permanent competing panels.
- **"AI magic" email products:** AI destinations, sparkle icons, generated summaries presented as fact, fabricated contact enrichment, automation that acts without a preview.
- **Superhuman feature-parity clone:** Superhuman is the visual and interaction reference for browsing (layout, density, type, keyboard feel), and close look parity there is a goal. Features and workflows are our own; don't import Superhuman's product scope or claim verified behavioral parity.
- **Generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics:** card stacks and grids, gradient heroes, oversized rounded panels, decorative illustration or motion.
- **Optimistic UI that lies:** "Done" before the provider confirmed, silent retries of ambiguous sends, dead controls that look actionable.

## Design Principles

1. **Honest state over smooth feel.** When speed and truthfulness conflict, show the truth. Every action has a visible pending, success, partial, failed, or unknown state. Show evidence and coverage, including unknown and retained facts.
2. **Keyboard first, mouse welcome.** Every core triage path is reachable and discoverable from the keyboard; pointer interaction is supported, never required.
3. **Content is the interface.** Chrome stays quiet and compact so the list and the conversation dominate. Add UI only when it earns its space in the triage loop; reuse established commands, navigation and recovery surfaces before adding new ones.
4. **Preview before power.** Bulk actions, automations, and agent-proposed changes show what they will do before they do it, and report exactly what they did after. Focus, bulk selection and message identity stay separate concepts.
5. **Opinionated defaults, replaceable parts.** Ship one strong way of working; design surfaces so views, signals, and commands can be swapped without breaking the core experience.

Standing constraints: ordinary reading stays local and non-mutating; message content renders as safe literal plain text; drafts stay local-only.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

Not a formal priority at this stage; no WCAG conformance target or certification is implied. Keyboard operability and visible focus remain required because they are core to the keyboard-first model. Don't regress behavior that already exists (explicit action labels, editable/IME shortcut protection, reduced-motion alternatives, selection/outcome announcements). The existing desktop/contact breakpoints remain authoritative; no new mobile UI. Revisit if the audience expands beyond the author.

> **Additional context needed**: quality bar and shipping constraints.

Polish is refinement, never concealed redesign. Preserve the incumbent visual world, content, behavior, and everything outside scope. If the concept itself is wrong, say so and recommend redesign or `bolder` instead of smuggling in a replacement.

A detector result is defect evidence, not proof of quality. Inspect the rendered experience and real interaction path.

## 1. Establish the system

Read DESIGN.md and representative tokens, shared components, patterns, and neighboring flows. If no formal system exists, use coherent project conventions.

Classify each drift before fixing it:

- **missing token:** the system needs a reusable value;
- **one-off implementation:** an existing shared component or pattern should replace it;
- **conceptual mismatch:** the flow, information architecture, or hierarchy differs from comparable product areas;
- **local defect:** the implementation is simply incomplete or inconsistent.

Fix the cause at the narrowest correct level. Ask when a binding system principle cannot be inferred.

## 2. Gather the evidence

Use the feature yourself at the surface's representative sizes: desktop and mobile on the web; on a native platform (`ios` / `android` / `adaptive`), the shipped device classes on the simulator, emulator, or hardware, captured per the platform reference's Verifying the build section. Determine:

- whether the path is functionally complete;
- the intended quality bar and time available;
- known constraints or deliberately unfinished work;
- the states, content lengths, roles, and input methods users will actually encounter.

If a prior critique exists, use it as one input:

```bash
.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable critique-storage latest "<resolved target>" --json
```

Exit 0 returns JSON with the latest snapshot's `body` and an exact `snapshot_file` identity. Retain `snapshot_file` until the end of the pass. For a local file target, the helper compares the file's exact current content fingerprint with the fingerprint captured by critique. Unchanged staged, unstaged, or untracked content remains current; any byte change, deletion, or replacement with a non-file closes the backlog it identified while preserving its trend history and exits 2. A URL target has no local fingerprint and remains current until explicitly closed. When current, incorporate relevant P0/P1 findings from `body` and name the snapshot read. Exit 2 means none exists or the target changed. Perform an independent pass either way.

## 3. Triage

Separate functional defects from cosmetic ones and fix in this order:

1. broken or blocked tasks, data loss, misleading state, and inaccessible paths;
2. missing loading, empty, error, success, disabled, and permission states;
3. flow, hierarchy, responsive, and design-system drift;
4. visual and motion inconsistencies;
5. code and asset cleanup.

Do not perfect one corner while leaving the rest below the same quality bar.

## 4. Polish the whole path

### Flow and hierarchy

- Match neighboring mental models, terminology, disclosure, routing, save behavior, and optimistic or pessimistic patterns.
- Make the primary task and current state obvious without flattening every element to equal weight.
- Ensure arrival, transition, empty, and recovery paths connect instead of behaving as isolated screens.

### Layout and type

- Align to the project's grid and spacing scale; fix optical as well as mathematical alignment.
- Group related content tightly and separate distinct groups generously.
- Keep same-role typography consistent; test measure, wrapping, localization expansion, zoom, and font loading.
- Verify every supported viewport rather than correcting only the current screenshot.

### Color, imagery, and icons

- Use semantic tokens and stable color meanings across themes.
- Verify text, control, and focus contrast in every state.
- Keep icon families, stroke/weight, sizing, and optical alignment coherent.
- Prevent image layout shift; use correct aspect ratios, responsive sources, and useful alt text.

### Interaction and state

- Every control needs appropriate default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, and success behavior.
- Preserve visible keyboard focus, logical tab order, labels, and platform-appropriate touch targets.
- Keep motion coherent, interruptible, and performant. Do not add animation merely to make polish visible.
- Validate long, missing, localized, offline, slow, and permission-limited content where the product can encounter it.

### Content and code

- Keep terminology, capitalization, punctuation, and factual copy consistent. Ask before changing claims.
- Remove debug output, dead code, unused imports, obsolete styles, and polish-created duplication.
- Replace custom implementations with shared components where the system owns the pattern.
- Promote genuinely reusable values to tokens; do not create a system abstraction for one local exception.

## 5. Verify and finish

Walk the complete path again with mouse, keyboard, and touch where applicable. Check:

- mobile, intermediate, and wide layouts on the web; phone and tablet size classes in both supported orientations on native;
- loading, empty, error, success, disabled, long-content, and missing-content states;
- zoom, contrast, focus, semantics, and screen-reader names;
- console errors, layout shift, interaction latency, and image loading everywhere; supported browsers on the web; supported OS versions, runtime warnings, and dropped frames on native;
- agreement with DESIGN.md, neighboring features, and the user's scope.

Follow the quality guidance supplied by `impeccable context` and hooks, then run any other relevant QA commands. Context requests a manual scan only when no automatic detector is active; never add another detector pass. Fix real defects and document only narrow intentional exceptions. A clean scan does not replace visual judgment.

Finish with a source diff: remove accidental churn, orphaned code, redundant values, and temporary artifacts. Ship only when the feature is functionally complete and consistently finished across the path.

When this pass clears every Priority Issue it took from a snapshot, close that snapshot:

```bash
.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable critique-storage close "<resolved target>" "<snapshot_file returned by latest>"
```

This closes only the snapshot this pass actually processed; if a newer critique landed meanwhile, its backlog stays live. Do not close when no snapshot was read, when `snapshot_file` was not retained, or when Priority Issues remain.
Typography carries information, hierarchy, and voice. Improve it inside the established visual world; do not replace the identity unless the user asked to.

---

## Visitor mode

- **Persuade + Experience:** display type may carry the voice. Use decisive contrast and responsive scale when the composition benefits.
- **Operate + Read:** stability, scanability, and measure come first. A single well-tuned family and fixed role scale are often right.
- **Native:** follow [ios.md](ios.md) or [android.md](android.md), including platform scaling and accessibility behavior.

If typography replacement would create a new identity, route through [new-work.md](new-work.md) and update DESIGN.md. Otherwise preserve confirmed families and improve their use.

## Two isolated assessments

When a sub-agent tool is available and permitted, run these independently; otherwise run them yourself in this order. Do not let detector findings anchor the design assessment.

1. **Typographic assessment:** inspect representative pages and styles. Answer every question below with a file, selector, or computed value:
   - **Authority and fit:** Which faces, weights, and roles are established? Do they fit the product and selected world, or are they unexamined defaults? Is every family necessary?
   - **Hierarchy:** Can heading, body, label, metadata, and data roles be distinguished at a glance? Are adjacent sizes or weights too close to carry different jobs?
   - **Scale and consistency:** Is there a deliberate role scale, or a collection of arbitrary values? Do repeated roles stay identical across screens and states?
   - **Reading:** Does body copy stay within a comfortable 45–75 character measure? Are line height, paragraph rhythm, contrast, and tracking tuned to the actual face, width, language, and surface?
   - **Stress:** What happens with long headings, localization expansion, zoom, narrow containers, missing weights, and font fallback?
   - **Delivery:** Are only used assets loaded? Do fallback metrics, loading strategy, and variable-font settings avoid invisible text and disruptive reflow?
2. **Mechanical scan:** run:

```bash
.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable detect --json --scope type [target files or dirs]
```

Also inspect dynamic or arbitrary font values the detector cannot interpret. Synthesize both assessments before editing, noting what each caught alone. A clean scan is a floor, not proof of good typography.

## Set the system

Before editing, state:

- the roles the interface needs;
- the intended contrast between those roles;
- the reading measure and density;
- which existing faces and weights are authoritative;
- any performance, localization, or accessibility constraints.

Use the fewest roles and families that make the hierarchy unmistakable. Combine size, weight, space, and tone deliberately instead of asking size alone to do all the work. Role names and tokens should describe purpose rather than values.

## Apply

- Keep body copy comfortably readable and zoomable. Use 1rem / 16px as the ordinary web body floor unless a dense role, platform convention, or user setting justifies otherwise.
- Keep prose in the 45–75ch range. Tune line height inversely with measure: wider lines generally need more leading.
- Compensate light text on dark surfaces on all three perceptual axes: slightly more line height, a touch more tracking, and one step more weight when the face needs it.
- Tune line height to the face, width, language, and contrast, not a universal ratio.
- Keep repeated roles consistent across screens and states.
- Use numeric, tabular, code, and label features when their content benefits.
- Load only used font assets and weights. Provide metric-compatible fallbacks and avoid blocking text.
- Let marketing display type respond to available space when useful; keep dense product and reading surfaces spatially predictable.
- Preserve browser zoom, user font settings, Dynamic Type, and platform text scaling.
- Use paragraph spacing or first-line indentation as the primary paragraph rhythm; combining both usually double-marks the boundary.

Do not make type decorative at the expense of comprehension, or introduce a second family without a clear role it alone can perform.

## Line breaks

After Matthew Butterick's *Practical Typography*, paraphrased; where his numbers differ from these, these stand.

- Set `text-wrap: balance` on headings and short centered blocks, and `text-wrap: pretty` on body copy. Both are progressive: a browser that ignores them keeps its default wrap.
- `pretty` pulls a word down beside a lone last word. It does not fill the last line, and a two-word tail is fine.
- In a column too narrow for either to help, edit the copy or widen the column.
- Break a heading by hand only between phrases, and check the break at every width the heading renders at. A hard break that lands mid-line on a phone is worse than the default wrap.
- An uneven break can carry meaning: a headline that lands on one word for weight, a poster line, a pull quote. Make it deliberate with a hard break or a wrap set on that element, and keep it rare. The detector's `straggler` and `unbalanced-heading` findings are advisory for this reason; say which breaks are intended.

## Verify

- Primary, secondary, body, and metadata roles are recognizable without reading the copy.
- Long text remains comfortable across relevant widths and languages.
- The typography belongs to the product and its established world.
- Loading does not create disruptive reflow or invisible text.
- Zoom, text scaling, focus, contrast, and reduced viewport paths remain usable.
- The final mechanical scan has no unexplained findings.

Answer each item with rendered or source evidence, then rerun the scan. Do not substitute a bare “yes” for verification.

When the hierarchy holds, hand off to `/impeccable polish`.

## Live-mode signature params

Every variant declares a coarse `scale` parameter and authors its type ramp against `var(--p-scale, 1)`.

```json
{"id":"scale","kind":"range","min":0.85,"max":1.3,"step":0.05,"default":1,"label":"Scale"}
```

Add at most one pairing or weight parameter when it represents a real system choice. Follow [live.md](live.md)'s parameter contract.
# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here except a line marked as a ban; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.

<script setup lang="ts">
/**
 * Plain-text, keyboard-first conversation reader (UX-02). Opening is read-only —
 * never marks read.
 *
 * Visit-scoped message state (active message, expansion, details disclosure,
 * scroll anchor) lives inside this mounted reader instance, keyed by
 * account+conversation reference and message ID — never by array position. It
 * survives J/K round trips and same-reference background replacements within
 * the reader session and is released when the reader closes (component
 * unmount) or the account changes.
 *
 * Archive/read controls are shown only when the authoritative capability permits them, and
 * Gmail-supplied plain-text limitations are disclosed explicitly (`unsupportedReason`,
 * `contextComplete === false`) instead of silently dropping content.
 *
 * Safety: message content is rendered exclusively through text interpolation
 * ({{ }}). No v-html, no markdown/HTML processing, no remote assets anywhere in
 * this slice — hostile markup stays literal text. Reply preparation always
 * targets the explicitly displayed latest message, never the focused message.
 *
 * Message commands (N/P/O/Shift+O, details dismissal) are exposed as narrow
 * methods for App's single keyboard dispatcher — this component never adds its
 * own window listener.
 */
import { actionLabel } from '../lib/browsing-actions';
import { compactDateLabel, fullDateLabel, machineDateTime } from '../lib/browsing-dates';
import { messageSnippet } from '../lib/message-snippet';
import { bodyNeedsMonospace, splitMessageBody, type MessageBodyParts } from '../lib/message-body-format';
import { computed, nextTick, reactive, ref, useId, watch } from 'vue';
import HeaderGlyph from './HeaderGlyph.vue';
import MessageAttachments from './MessageAttachments.vue';
import { useAttachmentTransfer } from '../composables/useAttachmentTransfer';
import type { Address, Conversation, ConversationRef, DraftSource, MailClient, MailError, Message } from '../lib/ipc/client';
import type { AttachmentDescriptor } from '../lib/ipc/generated';
import type { DetailState } from '../composables/useMailbox';

const props = defineProps<{
  conversation: Conversation | null;
  state: DetailState;
  error: MailError | null;
  commandInFlight: boolean;
  reminderEnabled?: boolean;
  /** The conversation reference the shell currently wants displayed. */
  openRef: ConversationRef | null;
  /**
   * Target identity from the list's own row, shown while the target loads and
   * no previous conversation is held. Never message content.
   */
  loadingIdentity?: { subject: string; sender: string | null; at: string | null } | null;
  /** Gmail mode: archive/unarchive controls are hidden, not just disabled. */
  readOnly?: boolean;
  browsingOnly?: boolean;
  navigationUnavailable?: boolean;
  showReadControls?: boolean;
  /** Nonzero: shared controls dispatch to the SELECTION (§3.3), so the reader
   * offers explicit count-labelled desired-state controls instead of the open
   * conversation's single-state toggles (mixed selections included). */
  selectionCount?: number;
  selectionContext?: 'inbox' | 'saved' | 'done' | 'starred' | 'search';
  /** Header slots the quiet icon actions are teleported into; inline when null. */
  backHost?: HTMLElement | null;
  actionsHost?: HTMLElement | null;
  /** J/K availability; undefined hides the previous/next chevrons. */
  canMovePrev?: boolean;
  canMoveNext?: boolean;
  /** Inline attachment rows: without a client the reader shows none. */
  client?: MailClient;
  /** Browser preview: saves are modelled in memory and say so. */
  preview?: boolean;
}>();

const emit = defineEmits<{
  close: [];
  /** Previous (-1) / next (+1) conversation, same path as K / J. */
  move: [delta: number];
  attachments: [origin: HTMLElement];
  archive: [];
  remind: [];
  unarchive: [];
  setRead: [read: boolean];
  prepareReply: [source: DraftSource];
  /** Identity of the message that currently owns reader focus. */
  activeMessage: [messageId: string | null];
  /** Hover/focus participant context override; `null` restores the baseline. */
  contactOverride: [
    override:
      | { ref: ConversationRef; messageId: string; displayName: string | null; mailbox: string }
      | null,
  ];
}>();

const container = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null);
const scrollerEl = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null);
const messageEls = new Map<string, HTMLElement>();

/** Selected-scope toolbar mode: nonzero selection dispatches to the whole
 * selection with explicit count labels (§3.3); null keeps single behavior. */
const bulkScope = computed(() =>
  (props.selectionCount ?? 0) > 0
    ? { count: props.selectionCount!, context: props.selectionContext ?? 'inbox' }
    : null,
);

type StarCoverage = NonNullable<Conversation['stars']>;

/** Short visible star line; exact coverage moves to the title/description. */
function starSummary(stars: StarCoverage): string {
  if (stars.starredMessages > 0) return stars.knownMessages < stars.totalMessages ? 'Starred (partial)' : 'Starred';
  return stars.knownMessages === stars.totalMessages && stars.totalMessages > 0 ? 'Not starred' : 'Star state unknown';
}

/** The line appears only with news: starred, incomplete coverage, or a pending
 * action (the effective value may then include unconfirmed intent). */
function starLine(conversation: NonNullable<typeof props.conversation>): { text: string; attention: boolean } | null {
  const stars = conversation.stars;
  if (!stars) return null;
  const complete = stars.totalMessages > 0 && stars.knownMessages === stars.totalMessages;
  const pending = Boolean(conversation.pendingOperationId);
  if (stars.starredMessages === 0 && complete && !pending) return null;
  return { text: starSummary(stars) + (pending ? ' (unconfirmed)' : ''), attention: !complete || pending };
}

function starCoverageDetail(stars: StarCoverage): string {
  return `Effective star values known for ${stars.knownMessages} of ${stars.totalMessages} cached messages. Pending intent is not provider confirmation.`;
}

const latestMessage = computed(() => props.conversation?.messages.at(-1) ?? null);
const replyBlockedReason = computed(() => {
  if (!props.conversation || !latestMessage.value) return 'No displayed latest message is available as a reply source.';
  if (props.conversation.retainedSnapshotAt) return 'Reply preparation is blocked for a retained snapshot; current message headers cannot be verified.';
  if (props.conversation.contextComplete === false) return 'Reply preparation is blocked because this cached conversation is incomplete.';
  if (props.conversation.replyContext && props.conversation.replyContext.sourceMessageId !== latestMessage.value.id) return 'Reply preparation is blocked because cached reply headers do not match the displayed latest message.';
  return null;
});

const replySourceId = `reader-reply-source-${useId()}`;
const replyTargetLabel = computed(() => latestMessage.value
  ? `Reply targets the latest message from ${latestMessage.value.from.displayName ?? latestMessage.value.from.mailbox}`
  : '');
/** Conversation-specific actions exist only for a ready conversation. */
const actionable = computed(() => props.state === 'ready' && !!props.conversation);
/**
 * A previous conversation kept on screen while the J/K target loads. It is
 * display only: nothing in it is actionable as if it were the open thread.
 */
const held = computed(() => props.state === 'loading' && !!props.conversation && keyOfDisplayed() === null);
/** Header actions stay mounted (disabled, not removed) for as long as a conversation is open. */
const actionsShown = computed(() => props.openRef !== null || actionable.value);
const hasMetaRow = computed(() => {
  if (!(actionable.value || held.value)) return false;
  return !!(props.readOnly || props.showReadControls || bulkScope.value);
});

/** The one rule for whether Prepare reply may run (button, glyph and the R key). */
function canPrepareReply(): boolean {
  return actionable.value && !props.browsingOnly && !!latestMessage.value && replyBlockedReason.value === null;
}

/** Title for the reply controls: the action label with its key, plus the target. */
const replyTitle = computed(() => {
  if (!actionable.value) return actionLabel('reply');
  return replyBlockedReason.value ?? `${actionLabel('reply')}. ${replyTargetLabel.value}`;
});

/** The standing guarantee behind the status line (hook per mode); Cached Trash has its own line and only names the mode. */
const readerStatus = computed(() => {
  // Cached Trash keeps its own line below; the status span only names the mode,
  // with no standing sentence or hook.
  if (props.browsingOnly) return { hook: undefined, word: 'Read-only', sentence: null };
  if (props.readOnly) {
    return {
      hook: 'reader-readonly',
      word: 'Read-only',
      sentence: 'Read-only Gmail view: messages are never marked as read. Opening this conversation does not change read state.',
    };
  }
  if (props.showReadControls) {
    return {
      hook: 'reader-no-auto-read',
      word: null,
      sentence: 'Opening this conversation does not change read state; use an explicit read control.',
    };
  }
  return null;
});

function prepareReply(): void {
  // Reply always targets the explicitly displayed latest message; focusing an
  // older message never changes the reply contract.
  const conversation = props.conversation;

This skill gives you the tools and permission to make design that earns the name out-of-distribution craft. Work as an award-winning design director would: production-grade code, a clear POV, a deep grasp of what the client and its users need, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Finish the job. No hedging, no shortcuts: the deliverable is complete, except assets the user must provide.
- Scale ambition to the surface's mode (see Modes). Persuade and Experience get full commitment: bold, distinct work with a point of view. On Operate and Read, ambition shows as precision and restraint, and patterns the visitor already knows earn their place.
- Verify by looking at the rendered result at the sizes it ships at, and batch the checks: fix what one look shows before looking again, rather than screenshotting after every tweak.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

**Launcher unavailable:** On refusal or failure, send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, including reading [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Loaded symbols stay out of the decoration.** A subject's world does not license emblems tied to militarism, supremacy, or hate movements as motifs, badges, or ornament, such as the Rising Sun flag's rays, the Confederate battle flag, or Nazi-era insignia and their stylised variants; reach for that world's neutral forms instead. Content that documents such a symbol as fact stays as it is.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. ### Purpose

Resolve one stable target, run two independent assessments, synthesize a design critique, persist a snapshot, and ask the user what to improve next. The chat response is the primary deliverable; the snapshot is an archive of that run.

### Hard Invariants

- Assessment A (design review) and Assessment B (detector/browser evidence) are both required, except on a native platform (see Assessment Orchestration).
- Assessment A and B MUST run as two isolated sub-agents whenever a sub-agent/Task tool is exposed. Running them inline in this context is "possible" but is NOT permitted; it is a degraded run. Inline is allowed ONLY when no sub-agent tool exists (or the user declined, on harnesses that ask). Native platforms run A alone (see Assessment Orchestration).
- If you degrade for any reason, the report's first line MUST be a banner: `⚠️ DEGRADED: single-context (<reason>)`. A silent degraded critique is a failed critique.
- Assessment A must finish before detector findings enter the parent synthesis context. Detector output is deterministic, but it still anchors judgment.
- A skipped detector is a failed critique run unless `impeccable detect` is missing or crashes after a real attempt, or the platform is native (see Assessment Orchestration).
- Viewable targets require browser inspection when available.
- Any local server started only for critique visualization must run in the background, have a recorded stop method, and be stopped before final reporting unless the user asks to keep it.
- Do not claim a user-visible overlay exists unless script injection succeeded and the detector ran in the page.
- The question is the LAST thing in the response. Write the entire report out first, then ask; nothing follows the question. Prose emitted after a structured question is withheld until the user answers it, so a report written after the question reads as if the critique never ran.

1. **Resolve the target** to a concrete file path or URL. Prefer a source path over a dev-server URL when both identify the same surface; ports drift, paths do not.

**Native platforms** (`ios` / `android` / `adaptive`): Assessment B does not apply, because `impeccable detect` and the browser overlay read only web markup. Run Assessment A alone in this context and skip both sub-agent gates below, the Codex permission question included: with no B there is nothing to isolate A from, so this is the complete native method and carries no degraded banner. Do not run `impeccable detect` on native source; its empty result reads as clean.

Delegate Assessment A and Assessment B to separate sub-agents. They must not see each other's output. Do not show findings to the user until synthesis.

Sub-agent gate (all harnesses):
- Unless a harness-specific gate below overrides this, spawn A and B as two isolated, parallel sub-agents whenever a sub-agent/Task tool is exposed. This is the default and is mandatory; do not run them inline because it is faster.
- Desktop apps (see **Desktop apps** under Assessment B) are the one exception to parallel: both sub-agents would drive the app's single window at once. Seed the window, spawn A, wait until it has finished and put the window back, then spawn B. They are still two isolated sub-agents, so this is not the degraded path.
- "Unavailable" means exactly one thing: no sub-agent/Task tool is exposed in this session (or, on harnesses that ask, the user declined). It does not mean inconvenient.
- If and only if sub-agents are unavailable, fall back sequentially: finish and record Assessment A, then run Assessment B, then synthesize, and emit the degraded banner.
- Whichever path you take, declare it in the report header (see Report header provenance). Skipping sub-agents without the banner is the most common failure of this command.

If browser automation is available, each assessment creates its own new tab. Never reuse an existing tab, even if it is already at the right URL. Desktop apps are the exception (see **Desktop apps** under Assessment B).

Read relevant source files and visually inspect the live page when browser automation is available. Think like a design director.

Evaluate:
- **Design specificity**: Is the composition, interaction, and visual language grounded in this product, or could an unrelated product use it unchanged? Make this judgment before seeing detector output.
- **Holistic design**: hierarchy, IA, emotional fit, discoverability, composition, typography, color, accessibility, states, copy, and edge cases.
- **Cognitive load**: consult the [Cognitive Load Assessment](#cognitive-load-assessment) section below; report checklist failures and decision points with >4 visible options.
- **Emotional journey**: peak-end rule, emotional valleys, reassurance at high-stakes moments.
- **Nielsen heuristics**: consult the [Heuristics Scoring Guide](#heuristics-scoring-guide) section below; score all 10 heuristics 0-4, marking any heuristic the mode-applicability rule allows as `n/a` instead of forcing a number.

### Assessment B: Detector + Browser Evidence

Run the bundled detector and browser visualization evidence. On web, Assessment B is mandatory and must remain isolated from Assessment A until both are complete.

CLI scan:
```bash
.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable detect --json [target]
```

- Pass markup files/directories as `[target]`; do not pass CSS-only files.
- For URLs, skip CLI scan and use browser visualization.
- For very large trees (500+ scannable files), narrow scope or ask.
- Exit code 0 = clean; 2 = findings.
- If the detector entrypoint is missing or fails to load, report deterministic scan unavailable and continue with browser/manual review.

Browser visualization is required for a viewable target when browser automation is available. Use a localhost dev/static URL for local files; avoid `file://` unless the available browser explicitly supports this workflow. Overlay flow:

1. Create a fresh tab and navigate. Prefer the harness's native/browser-canvas screenshot path before hand-rolling a Playwright/Puppeteer script; only fall back to a custom script when no native browser tool is exposed.
2. Preflight mutable injection by setting `document.title` and appending a `<script>` tag. Read-only evaluate APIs do not count.
3. If mutation is unavailable, skip live server, browser presentation, and injection; report fallback signal.
4. If mutation is available, start `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable live-server --background`, present the browser if supported, label `[Human]`, scroll top, inject `http://localhost:PORT/detect.js`, wait 2-3 seconds, read `impeccable` console messages, then run `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable live-server stop --keep-inject`. 5. For multi-view targets, inject on 3-5 representative pages.

**Desktop apps** (Electron, NW.js, CEF, WebView2): there is no URL to open, so Assessment B attaches to the running app instead.

1. Launch the app with a local DevTools port: `--remote-debugging-port=9222` (Electron, NW.js, CEF), or `REDACTED` for WebView2. Keep the port on 127.0.0.1 and never expose it beyond this machine; prefer a test profile and test data.
2. Seed the state under review (route, open panel, theme, data). The scan reads the window as it stands. Keep the window on screen: a minimized or hidden window scans without the pixel contrast reads.
3. Run `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable detect --cdp 9222 --target <part of the page URL or title> --json`. It returns the same JSON as a URL scan and leaves the page as found. With several pages open it fails and lists them; rerun with a `--target` that names one.
4. Take screenshots through the harness's CDP tooling (`Page.captureScreenshot` on the same target). Skip the live-server overlay: there is no `[Human]` tab.

The app has one window, so the assessments take turns in it instead of opening tabs (A, then B; see the sub-agent gate), and each must leave it as found: put back any route, scroll, theme, or panel it changed. Tauri on macOS (WKWebView) and on Linux (WebKitGTK) expose no CDP: run Assessment A and the source scan only, and say so in Run Notes.
